era: Bright retro-future: a space age imagined as the present, built as high art, optimistic and immaculate.

concept_prompt.era: Optimistic atompunk city in an alternate history: a 1950s world that discovered atomic power centuries ago, so its culture and style are 1950s but its technology is centuries ahead: 1950s-styled robots, trams and street furniture doing super-advanced things. Atomic power made energy, travel and building cheap: sky rail, skyports, towers and liners, everything physical abundant. Thinking machines and networks never came: robots are clockwork-smart on fixed routines, and records are physical (microfilm, punch cards, pneumatic tubes, stamped forms). An abundant, orderly city that runs on routine and paperwork.
concept_prompt.city: Streamline Moderne, Art Deco and Googie. Cream limestone and ivory enamel buildings with seafoam-teal faience bands, chrome sphere finials, banners on lamp posts, planted terraces, cypress and palms, parasol café terraces, pale cream stone paving with seafoam inlay bands, soft lilac-grey asphalt, thin brushed-brass hairline trim, coral and peach accents. Warm afternoon sun, soft shadows, soft blue sky. Clean, prosperous, graceful; people in the city's space-age couture. Cinematic painted concept art with photographic material realism.
concept_prompt.rule: Every concept generation starts from this block (era, city, avoid) and an open brief: the art designs, and look decisions come from it. deltaE and checker rules gate what the art proposes; they are not the source of options. A decision taken from art cites the image and its prompt (PROVENANCE.json beside the images). Tools: Codex CLI image tool (ChatGPT plan), Runware (Qwen Image 2.1).
concept_prompt.source: era: GDD §01 world (Sky, 2026-10-14; brief 008 Era) and the era sentence of the accepted prompts; city and avoid: the prompts Sky accepted, briefs/009/concepts/PROVENANCE.json (2026-10-14), minus each frame's view and subject; grime and present-day street furniture added (Sky, 2026-10-14).

all: No text, logos or watermarks in the image.
meta: No living artist names in prompts.
No environment surface uses a signal colour at full strength.

guide: People wear space-age couture as everyday clothing: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further. Any role, civilian, worker, officer or agent, wears it; the job shows through cut, colour and one telling detail (a slim chrome holster, an earpiece, a tool, a satchel), never through costume, tactical kit or matching uniforms.

Couture details, one or two per person, never all, never the same pair twice on one sheet: visor glasses, a stand-up ribbed collar, glossy vinyl, bonded wool, silver lame or brushed-metal trim, a geometric cut-out, circles or chevrons, chunky geometric jewellery, a tabard over a fitted tunic, a transparent bubble umbrella or hatbox; only rarely a moulded dome or helmet hat. Garments and footwear follow the person.

Colours on cream: seafoam teal, coral red, vermilion, mustard gold, white and silver, with navy and black for contrast; one dominant block per person, chosen for who they are, so a group never matches.
Cast: mix ages, builds, genders and ethnicities unless the brief fixes them.
Security and institutions dress sleeker: white, black, gold and chrome couture with armour accents.

Agents, special ops and other hard trades read as what they are at a glance, still in the city's space-age couture: darker colour blocks from the city palette (navy, black, chrome, with coral, teal or gold) on the same details as everyone else, visor glasses, stand-up ribbed collars, glossy vinyl, geometric cuts, brushed-metal trim, and the tools of the trade worn like jewellery; never present-day leather, tactical kit or matching kit.

Only when the brief is about the player cell: visitors from a nearby timeline, the same world a few decades on; sleeker and more technical than the crowd, fitted layers and sharp geometric lines, black, cream and gold with a violet accent, one signature piece each.

The city: cream limestone, teal and mint enamel, chrome fixtures, coral transit, palms and long soft shadows; grandeur over detail at Space Age Expo scale; towers, rockets, ringed planets and faded daytime moons on the skyline.

palette_world.status: current, tuneable: Sky reviews it in the world (2026-10-14)
palette_world.rule: Pastel cream and peach base for ground, stone and bodies; saturated enamel accents (cobalt, flamingo, sunshine, mint, turquoise) on panels, awnings, signs, roofs and trim, never whole buildings; lagoon water; coral transit. Brass, not gold, at street level and on facades; skyline crowns keep gold; gold or brass only as hairline, frame, bead and small metal, never a large surface. Every world colour at least deltaE2000 20 from each signal colour, measured on the unlit palette.

gold_trim.why: gold_trim #c9a24f is deltaE2000 10.2 from guard #f0a020. Since v0.19.0 (Sky: brass, not gold, at street level and on facades) world surfaces use brass #99784d (21.3 from guard), the same as roles.trim, roles.accent_gold and facade.json paletteOverride.gold_trim (the sign boards). No kit material reads it now: tools/decokit mats.py GOLD_TRIM is unused, DK_Gold17 is light brass #ad866f (21.3) and the crowns' gold is DK_Crown_Gold17 #c9c08e

signal_colours.rule: No environment surface uses a signal colour at full strength; each signal also has a shape or motion cue. Signals render unlit and emissive and outside the post grade (the grade shifts them deltaE 4-10), so neither light nor grade shifts them: a signal never depends on the light; the deltaE2000 >= 20 gate applies to the unlit palette against the signal colours. One exception (Sky, 2026-10-14: 'red is definitely ok for electronics displays'): a small emissive pictogram on an electronic display (a crossing signal's stop figure) may be red, even within deltaE 20 of the cones; never a surface; the cones keep their own shape and motion cue.

materials: saturated vitreous enamel panels (cobalt, flamingo, sunshine, mint, turquoise)
warm brass trim at street level and on facades, gold on skyline crowns

character.label: Character
character.line: A character turnaround sheet: one person drawn front, three-quarter, side and back at the same scale, full body head to toe, relaxed A-pose with the arms a little away from the body and nothing loose below the hip. Dressed in space-age couture: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further, tailored, chic and wearable, never astronaut suits or fancy dress.

finish.look: Gouache and marker rendering in the tradition of 1960s fashion illustration and costume design boards, crisp confident linework, soft studio light, material realism. Plain warm-cream backdrop, clear margin all round.

model.label: Model sheet
model.use: Finished front, side, back sheet for 3D.
model.line: A finished character model sheet for a 3D artist: the same person drawn front, side and back, orthographic with no perspective, side by side at exactly the same height on one baseline, neutral A-pose with the arms about 30 degrees from the body, hands open, feet slightly apart, neutral face. Every garment, seam, panel, trim and material is resolved and identical across the three views. Dressed in space-age couture: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further, tailored, chic and wearable, never astronaut suits or fancy dress.
rules: The figure stands alone: nothing in the hands, no seated or action pose, nothing hiding the body outline, hair and clothes clear of the hands and feet.
A reference image is a rough concept: keep who the person is and what they wear, never its pose, linework or rendering.

finish.look: Finished production rendering, clean and painted: crisp edges, solid colour, every material legible (gloss vinyl, brushed chrome, matte wool, leather), flat even front light with no cast shadows and no haze. Plain light-grey backdrop, clear margin all round.

Dressed in space-age couture: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further, tailored, chic and wearable, never astronaut suits or fancy dress.
